pairs.why: Same pumpkin, but B's bright daytime sky with soft clouds matches the sunny, cheerful lighting of all the real garden cards, while A's night scene breaks that look.
Same pumpkin, but A sits in the bright daytime garden light the real cards use, while B moves it to a dark night sky.
B's saturated purple hat on light orange wood matches the bright, warm palette and light floors of the real cards; A's dark charcoal hat on dark wood reads gloomier and heavier.
A's vivid purple hat on light warm wood fits the real cards' bright palette and floor tone better than B's dull black hat on dark wood.
Per the lessons that real cards are smoother, B's softly shaded smooth wood matches the clean real finish better than A's busier carved wood grain, though both are close.
A's smoother, cleaner wood matches the real cards' finish better than B's more textured grain, though the difference is small.
B's saturated purple spider on a smooth soft base matches the real cards' clean, colorful finish, while A's stone base with cracks and moss is the texture-heavy look the lessons rejected.
A's bright purple spider on a smooth sand disc matches the real cards' smooth, colorful finish better than B's dark spider on a cracked, mossy stone base.
